`ciphey/iface/_modules.py` — `__ge__` (lines 199–200)

The function is `__ge__`, a method of the `DecoderComparer` class in `ciphey/iface/_modules.py`. It takes another `DecoderComparer` and calls `self.value.priority()` and `other.value.priority()`, where `value` is a `Type[Decoder]`. It returns the result of comparing the two with `>=`. It sits next to the related comparison methods `__le__`, `__lt__` and `__gt__`.

`ciphey/mathsHelper.py` — `new_sort` (lines 157–176)

The function is `new_sort`, a static method in `ciphey/mathsHelper.py`. It logs the incoming dictionary and calls `sorted(new_dict.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)` to order the items by value, highest first. It wraps the result in an `OrderedDict` so that order is kept, logs it, and returns it. Python's `sorted` is stable, even with `reverse=True`, so keys with equal values keep their original relative order.

`web3/_utils/module_testing/eth_module.py` — `test_eth_get_logs_with_logs_none_topic_args` (lines 4529–4537)

The function is `test_eth_get_logs_with_logs_none_topic_args`, a method in `web3/_utils/module_testing/eth_module.py` that takes `w3`. It builds a `FilterParams` dict with `"fromBlock": BlockNumber(0)` and `"topics": [None, None, None]`; the inline comment calls this "None overflowing". It passes the filter to `w3.eth.get_logs` and asserts `len(result) == 0`, so the test expects no logs back.

`web3/providers/persistent/persistent.py` — `_get_response_for_request_id` (lines 62–98)

The function is `_get_response_for_request_id`, an async method in `web3/providers/persistent/persistent.py`. It takes a `request_id` and an optional `timeout`, which falls back to `self.request_timeout` when not given. An inner coroutine, `_match_response_id_to_request_id`, builds a cache key with `generate_cache_key`. It then loops, calling `await asyncio.sleep(0)` on each pass to hand control back to the event loop, until that key appears in `self._request_processor._request_response_cache`; at that point it returns the response popped with `pop_raw_response`. The loop is wrapped in `asyncio.wait_for` with the timeout, and an `asyncio.TimeoutError` is turned into a `TimeExhausted` exception.

`locust/clients.py` — `rename_request` (lines 88–95)

The function is `rename_request` in `locust/clients.py`. It is a method decorated with `@contextmanager` that takes a string `name` and is annotated as returning `Generator[None, None, None]`; its docstring says it groups requests using the "with" keyword. It sets `self.request_name = name`, yields to run the body of the `with` block, and in a `finally` clause resets `self.request_name` to `None`. The reset therefore happens even if the block raises. It sets the label back to `None` rather than restoring whatever value it held before.

`locust/test/test_fasthttp.py` — `test_custom_ssl_context_fail_with_bad_context` (lines 208–228)

The function is `test_custom_ssl_context_fail_with_bad_context`, a test method in `locust/test/test_fasthttp.py`. It defines an inner factory, `create_custom_context`, which builds a context with `gevent.ssl.create_default_context()`, sets `check_hostname = True` and then sets `verify_mode = gevent.ssl.CERT_NONE`. It creates a `FastHttpSession` against `https://127.0.0.1:<port>`, passing that factory as `ssl_context_factory` and `user=None`. It then asserts that `s.get("/")` raises `ValueError` whose args are exactly `("Cannot set verify_mode to CERT_NONE when check_hostname is enabled.",)`.

`src/marshmallow/class_registry.py` — `register` (lines 28–67)

The function is `register` in `src/marshmallow/class_registry.py`. It takes a `classname` string and a class `cls`, reads `cls.__module__`, and builds a full path such as `module.classname`. It then records the class in the module-level `_registry` dict, which maps names to lists of classes. Under the simple class name, it appends `cls` only if no class from the same module is already listed, and creates a new list if the name is absent. Under the full path, it adds a new entry, or replaces an existing one with `[cls]`; it returns `None`.

`src/marshmallow/exceptions.py` — `normalized_messages` (lines 44–47)

The function is `normalized_messages`, a method on the exception class in `src/marshmallow/exceptions.py`. It takes no arguments besides `self`. If `self.field_name` equals `SCHEMA` and `self.messages` is already a `dict`, it returns `self.messages` unchanged. Otherwise it wraps the messages as `{self.field_name: self.messages}`, so the result is always a dictionary keyed by field name.

`mlc_llm/dispatch/dispatch_tir_operator_adreno.py` — `fused_fused_decode9_matmul7` (lines 1222–1261)

The function is `fused_fused_decode9_matmul7`, a TIR `T.prim_func` in `mlc_llm/dispatch/dispatch_tir_operator_adreno.py`. It takes a uint32 buffer `lv19` (512×22016), a float16 scale buffer `lv20` (128×22016) and a float16 input `lv1654` (1×1×4096), and writes the float16 output `var_matmul_intermediate` (1×1×22016). The "decode" block loops over a 4096×22016 grid. For each element it shifts `lv19[v_i // 8, v_j]` right by `(v_i % 8) * 4`, masks the result with 15, casts it to float16, subtracts 7 and multiplies by `lv20[v_i // 32, v_j]`, storing the value in the temporary `p_output0_intermediate`. The "matmul" block then reduces over `k` (4096): it initializes the output to 0 and accumulates `lv1654[v_i0, v_i1, v_k] * p_output0_intermediate[v_k, v_i2]` into the output buffer.

`mlc_llm/dispatch/llama/main.py` — `fused_decode4_matmul5_int3_fp16_before` (lines 5734–5751)

The function is `fused_decode4_matmul5_int3_fp16_before`, a TIR `@T.prim_func` in `mlc_llm/dispatch/llama/main.py`. It takes a (412, 4096) `uint32` buffer `lv1587`, a (103, 4096) `float16` scale buffer `lv1588`, a (1, 1, 4096) `float16` input `lv1520`, and a (1, 1, 4096) `float16` output `var_matmul_intermediate`. The "decode" block fills a (4096, 4096) `float16` intermediate. For each element it shifts `lv1587[i // 10, j]` right by `(i % 10) * 3` and masks with 7, which unpacks a 3-bit value. It then casts that value to `float16`, subtracts 3 and multiplies by `lv1588[i // 40, j]`. The "matmul" block sets the output to zero in `T.init()`, then accumulates `lv1520[i0, i1, k] * var_decode_intermediate[k, i2]` over `k`.

`src/openai/_models.py` — `_construct_field` (lines 245–257)

The function is `_construct_field` in `src/openai/_models.py`. It takes `value`, a `FieldInfo` called `field` and a string `key`. If `value` is `None`, it returns `field_get_default(field)`. Otherwise it gets the type from `field.annotation` when `PYDANTIC_V2` is true, or from `cast(type, field.outer_type_)` when it is not. It raises a `RuntimeError` ("Unexpected field type is None for {key}") if that type is `None`, and otherwise returns `construct_type(value=value, type_=type_)`.

`src/openai/cli/_api/audio.py` — `transcribe` (lines 64–78)

The function is `CLIAudio.transcribe`, a static method in `src/openai/cli/_api/audio.py` that takes `CLITranscribeArgs`. It opens `args.file` in binary mode and wraps its contents in a `BufferReader` labelled "Upload progress". It then calls `get_client().audio.transcriptions.create` with the file, `args.model`, and the optional `language`, `temperature` and `prompt` (each falling back to `NOT_GIVEN` when unset), plus `response_format` cast to `Any` for forwards-compatibility. Finally it shows the result with `print_model(model)`.

`src/black/nodes.py` — `is_part_of_annotation` (lines 977–979)

The function is `is_part_of_annotation` in `src/black/nodes.py`. It takes a `Leaf` and returns a `bool` that says whether the leaf is part of a type annotation. It calls `get_annotation_type(leaf)` and returns `True` when the result is not `None`. The visible tail of `get_annotation_type` walks up through `ancestor.parent`, can return `"param"`, and otherwise returns `None`.

`src/black/trans.py` — `_merge_string_group` (lines 586–639)

The function is `_merge_string_group`, a method in `src/black/trans.py`. It loops over `string_indices`, each the first leaf of a group of adjacent strings. Each group is checked with `self._validate_msg`, and groups that fail are skipped. Groups that pass are merged with `self._merge_one_string_group`, and the result is stored in `merged_string_idx_dict` as `{string_idx: (num_of_strings, string_leaf)}`. If nothing was merged, it returns `TErr("No string group is merged")`. Otherwise it builds a clone of the line: it appends each merged leaf at its start index, keeps only the comments (via `line.comments_after`) for the leaves the merge absorbed, copies all other leaves with `append_leaves`, and returns `Ok(new_line)`.

`torch_geometric/datasets/graph_generator/tree_graph.py` — `tree` (lines 11–49)

The function is `tree` in `torch_geometric/datasets/graph_generator/tree_graph.py`. It takes `depth`, `branch` (default 2), `undirected` (default False) and an optional `device` (default `None`, documented as the desired device of the returned tensors). It starts an `edges` list and a `depths` list holding `[0]` for the root. A nested recursive `add_edges` then appends `branch` child edges and child depths at each level below `depth`, and recurses into each child. Finally it builds `edge_index` with `torch.tensor(edges, device=device).t().contiguous()`, applies `to_undirected` with `num_nodes=len(depths)` if `undirected` is set, and returns `edge_index` together with a tensor of node depths.

`torch_geometric/explain/algorithm/captum.py` — `_to_edge_mask` (lines 174–176)

The function is `_to_edge_mask` in `torch_geometric/explain/algorithm/captum.py`. It takes an `edge_index` tensor and gets the number of edges from its second dimension (`edge_index.shape[1]`). It returns `torch.ones(num_edges, requires_grad=True, device=edge_index.device)`. That is a mask of all ones, so every edge starts out equally important; it tracks gradients and sits on the same device as the input.

`src/poetry/console/commands/init.py` — `_find_best_version_for_package` (lines 444–462)

The function is `_find_best_version_for_package`, a method in `src/poetry/console/commands/init.py`. It takes `name`, an optional `required_version`, an `allow_prereleases` flag (default `False`) and an optional `source`. It builds a `VersionSelector` over the pool from `self._get_pool()` and calls `find_best_candidate` with those arguments. If no package is found it raises `ValueError` ("Could not find a matching version of package ..."); otherwise it returns a tuple of `package.pretty_name` and `^` followed by `package.version.to_string()`.

`src/poetry/installation/installer.py` — `_write_lock_file` (lines 348–354)

The function is `_write_lock_file`, a method in `src/poetry/installation/installer.py`. It takes a `LockfileRepository` `repo` and an optional `force: bool = False`, and returns `None`. It acts only when `self.is_dry_run()` is false and either `force` or `self._update` is set. In that case it calls `self._locker.set_lock_data(self._package, repo.packages)`, and if that reports an update it prints a blank line followed by "Writing lock file" through `self._io.write_line`. The lines just before it (343–344) show the call `self._write_lock_file(lockfile_repo)`, commented as running only when installation succeeds.

`src/py/reactpy/reactpy/testing/backend.py` — `stop_server` (lines 124–127)

The function is `stop_server`, an async closure defined inside a method of the testing backend in `src/py/reactpy/reactpy/testing/backend.py`. It calls `server_future.cancel()` on the server task, which was created around `self.implementation.serve_development_app(...)`. It then awaits the task with `asyncio.wait_for(server_future, timeout=self.timeout)` inside `suppress(asyncio.CancelledError)`, so cleanup is bounded by the timeout and the expected cancellation error is swallowed. It takes no arguments and returns `None`; it is registered for teardown through `self._exit_stack.push_async_callback(stop_server)`.

`src/py/reactpy/reactpy/widgets.py` — `image` (lines 13–33)

The function is `image` in `src/py/reactpy/reactpy/widgets.py`. It takes a `format` string, a `value` that is a `str` or `bytes` (default `""`), and an optional `attributes` dict. A format of `"svg"` becomes `"svg+xml"`. A string value is encoded to bytes, and the bytes are base64-encoded with `b64encode` to build a `data:image/{format};base64,...` URL. It returns a `VdomDict` of the form `{"tagName": "img", "attributes": {"src": src, ...}}`, with any extra attributes merged in.
